For reproducibility, fix item-ID ordering, package versions, text cleaning and every vectorizer parameter; save the fitted vocabulary and IDF. `TfidfVectorizer` has no random-state parameter. Its default `token_pattern=r'(?u)\b\w\w+\b'` excludes single-character tokens; `(1,2)` adds bigrams, `min_df` removes rare terms, and `max_features` caps vocabulary by corpus term frequency. A proposed coverage-oriented starting point: `min_df=1`, bounded `max_features`, `dtype=float32`, L2 normalization; explicitly decide whether single-character tokens matter. Detect empty-vocabulary failures and zero rows rather than inventing lexical matches. [Vectorizer documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer.html), [implementation](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/main/sklearn/feature_extraction/text.py).

For bounded retrieval, retain CSR features and compute query batches against the catalog with `cosine_similarity(..., dense_output=False)`; L2-normalized dot products equal cosine similarity. Sparse products can still become dense, so bound batches conservatively or use catalog blocks with incremental top-k reduction; avoid a full catalog-square matrix. Alternatively, `pairwise_distances_chunked` supports immediate reduction under a working-memory target. Define ordering as descending similarity, then ascending item ID, resolving boundary ties before truncation; sorting an already truncated neighbor list cannot recover excluded ties. Scikit-learn warns that equal-distance neighbor selection depends on input ordering. [Cosine similarity](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.pairwise.cosine_similarity.html), [chunking](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.pairwise_distances_chunked.html), [neighbor ties](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/neighbors.html).

Coverage implication: after exclusions, exactly 99 positive-similarity neighbors exist only when at least 99 eligible items share retained terms. Zero vectors have no positive matches. Requiring 99 therefore drops sparse queries and biases coverage toward common vocabulary. Measure zero-row rate, eligible positive-neighbor counts and the fraction reaching 99; never interpret an arbitrary zero-similarity fill as lexical evidence.
